transcript.text: Alright, let's get the stability sprint planning underway. We've got a ten-business-day sprint with capacity for one primary technical-debt focus, and three candidates on the table: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our normal round-robin check-in. Backend engineering, security engineering, and customer support — please share your perspective on which of these three should be the priority and why. I'll make the final call once I've heard from all three.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet, but this means legacy_csv_exporter is nearly done and could be fully completed during this sprint.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a security finding before we go further. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was still verifying scanner results and hadn't filed the finding yet, but given Devon just indicated legacy_csv_exporter is nearly complete and could be finished this sprint, I think we should prioritize it — finishing the remaining two endpoints gives us a natural window to also bump libxml to 4.1.0 and close this vulnerability in the same sprint.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something important to add on legacy_csv_exporter. During a customer call this morning, I confirmed that exactly 42 enterprise accounts still depend on legacy_csv_exporter's old audit-column behavior. Those accounts need a migration guide before the new behavior is enabled. I recorded the call in a support note that hasn't synced to the sprint-planning system yet, so this wouldn't be visible to anyone else right now. If we prioritize legacy_csv_exporter this sprint, we need to account for producing that migration guide as part of the work — otherwise enabling the new behavior would break those 42 enterprise customers.
